human_questions.question: Is the mark under the het (line 04, second phrase) a patah stroke or two tsere dots? It looked like tsere (פַּחֵד) when zoomed, but the dots touch the baseline.
Under the het of the word after בְּאַרְקָא, is it hataf-patah (ֲ) or hataf-segol (ֱ)? The three dots plus sheva look like hataf-segol.

I see no yod and a qamatz under the lamed. Is the small mark below the lamed/mem a meteg, or is it only the hiriq? If there is no meteg, the candidate's U+05BD should be removed, giving בִּירוּשָׁלָ͏ִם.
Is there a holam dot over the right head of the צ in the first word, or none (צַר or unpointed צר)? I see no dot at this resolution.
Is the vowel under the resh of the first word a patah or a tsere? Zoomed, it looks like tsere (קָרֵב).
Under the shin, is it segol (קָדְשֶׁךָ) or sheva (קָדְשְׁךָ)?
Does the lamed carry qubuts, and does the yod carry a dagesh? I could not see either mark clearly. Is it גָּלֻיּוֹת, or גָּלְיוֹת/גָּלִיוֹת as printed?
Is the vowel under the he hataf-patah or segol? Does the yod have a dagesh?
Is the third consonant a nun or a bet (שׁוֹכְבִים)? Bet would match 'slumber'. Do not decide from the English; read the glyph.
Is the mark under the tet tsere or segol? Does the nun have a dagesh? It looked like segol without a nun-dagesh (יַטֶּנוּ).

There are small extra marks next to the vowels: under the alef of אֶרֶץ, under the qof of וְכִתְקֹעַ, and a vertical stroke beside the qamatz of תִּשְׁמָעוּ. Are these accents/meteg/silluq? If so, which ones, so they can be encoded?

Is the mark under the nun, beside the qubuts, a meteg/silluq-type accent? If so, which one?
